issues.description: The problem statement requires implementing config_system that accepts a pointer to a Config-Struct (problem_statement.md lines 21-22), but the solution implementation of config_system reads a raw integer from the call stack ([esp+4]) and the comment explicitly says it expects an integer, not a pointer (solution_repository/helloWorld.asm lines 6-10). This is a parameter/contract mismatch: students following the spec will write code that treats the argument as a pointer (and attempt to dereference it), while the provided solution (and any automated tests tied to it) treat the argument as an integer value. This discrepancy will confuse students about the intended calling convention and data layout and may cause incorrect student implementations or failing tests.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the parameter contract consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) Update the solution to accept a pointer to a Config-Struct (read the pointer from [esp+4], then dereference fields from that pointer), and add or document the expected Config struct layout; and add a short stub/comment in the template showing the config_system label and expected stack layout so students know how to implement it. Or (B) Change the problem statement to state that config_system accepts an integer value (not a pointer). Option A is recommended if the exercise intends to teach pointer/struct handling; Option B is acceptable if the intent is to pass a simple integer.
